title: Misleading Control Flow Documentation
pattern: Comments stating that a function executes a simple, unconditional behavior when it actually contains conditional escape paths or panics.
why_bad: Creates severe runtime failures. Callers design their systems assuming a safe loop return, but get hit with hard panics or exceptions due to the undocumented branch.
detection: Doc-comments using terms like 'always returns X' or 'returns when Y' on functions containing distinct control-flow branches, panic statements, or timeouts not described in the text.
counterexample: A doc-comment enumerating every exit path: 'Waits for the connection to close. Panics if the operation times out.'
fix: Align the comment text with all execution branches and boundary behaviors.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Bad Comments - Misleading Comments").
